Empirical probe (disposable worktree /tmp/probe-m3fu, removed): materialize → dirty file → teardown returns RetainedDirty → rm -rf worktree → rematerialize fails 'fatal: .../surfaces/01STALE/solo is a missing but already registered worktree; use add -f, or prune or remove' → second rematerialize fails identically (PERMANENTLY WEDGED). No existing test in tests/m3_execution.rs covers dirty-retain-then-delete; the covered retry path (t5) goes through a clean teardown whose 'git worktree remove' unregisters properly.
confirmed.confirmed_because:
Confirmed by code and probe. In /home/user/sergeant-rs/src/runtime/surface.rs the `git worktree prune` added by the F3 fix exists only inside `teardown_binding`'s missing-path branch (line 404); `rematerialize` (lines 326-367) calls `add_worktree_from` with no prune, no `-f`, and no handling of a registered-but-missing path, and src/runtime/engine.rs:530-537 propagates the SurfaceError straight out of `retry`, leaving the work in failed/blocked/waiting with §12's only door shut. Probe (fresh throwaway repo in the scratchpad — no mutation of the project tree, no git worktree added to it, directory deleted afterward; main tree verified clean and `git worktree list` shows only the checkout): `git worktree add -b sergeant/W1

` → `git worktree add

sergeant/W1` fails 'is a missing but already registered worktree' on the first AND second attempt (git 2.43.0 does not self-prune fresh stale entries), so retry is permanently wedged with no product path that prunes — only cancel reaches the pruning branch, and cancel is terminal. confirmed.axis: duplicate-repository submits rejected before any worktree exists (F1)
confirmed.summary: The F1 fix rejects duplicate repository NAMES (in sergeant.toml and in the submit selection) but not two distinct names resolving to the SAME repository path, so a same-path duplicate sails through plan() and is only stopped mid-materialize by the second 'git worktree add -b sergeant/<id>' failing — after the first binding already created a real worktree and branch in the user's repository, permanently leaving a sergeant/<work-id> branch behind (teardown retains branches by design) for a submission that was statically rejectable with zero side effects.
confirmed.evidence: Code: src/domain/workspace.rs from_config (lines 224-253) dedups on entry.name only while resolving each path through 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' — the resolved PathBuf is in hand but never checked for duplicates; select() (lines 287-316) likewise name-only. Empirical probe (disposable worktree, removed): config declaring name="a" path="solo" and name="b" path="solo/" parsed OK with both RepositorySpec.path equal; materialize returned PartialFailure ('cannot materialize work surface: ... branch sergeant/01SAMEPATH already exists' shape) and 'git show-ref refs/heads/sergeant/01SAMEPATH' in the USER's repo succeeded afterward — worktree created then torn down, branch left behind. The work does end blocked with the teardown journaled (fail-closed downstream), but F1's bar — rejected before any worktree exists — is bypassed for path-identity duplicates.
confirmed.confirmed_because: Verified by code reading plus a git probe. `Workspace::from_config` (src/domain/workspace.rs:224-253) dedups only on `entry.name` even though it holds the canonical `resolved` path from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and `select()` (287-316) is likewise name-only; `Engine::plan` (src/runtime/engine.rs:269-334) adds no further check, and neither `surface::materialize` nor the API does any path-identity dedup (grep for dedup/HashSet/duplicate over surface.rs, engine.rs, api.rs finds nothing relevant, and tests/m3_execution.rs has no same-path case). So two entries with distinct plain names resolving to one repo pass planning. A scratch-repo probe (throwaway repo in the scratchpad, not the project tree) confirms the runtime consequence: `git worktree add -b sergeant/01X <p1> HEAD` succeeds and creates the branch, then the second `git worktree add -b sergeant/01X <p2> HEAD` in the same repo fails with `fatal: a branch named 'sergeant/01X' already exists` while `refs/heads/sergeant/01X` remains present. In `materialize` that hits the PartialFailure path, which tears down the first worktree but retains its branch by design (surface.rs teardown contract), so the user's repository is left with a `sergeant/<work-id>` branch for a submission that was statically rejectable — exactly the ordering the F1 fix's own doc comment on `select()` says it exists to prevent ("the second `git worktree add` failing after the first has already touched the user's repository"). The outcome is fail-closed and journaled, which is why warning severity is right, but the finding's claim — the F1 bar is bypassed for path-identity duplicates — stands.

confirmed.summary: `a_crash_inside_the_submit_window_fails_closed_with_the_git_evidence` is flaky on a clean HEAD, failing at daemon startup — it produced two false 'mutation killed' results during my probing before I isolated it.
confirmed.evidence: On the unmodified probe worktree (`git checkout -- .` first) I ran `cargo test` six consecutive times; run 6 produced: `---- a_crash_inside_the_submit_window_fails_closed_with_the_git_evidence stdout ----` / `panicked at tests/m3_execution.rs:148:6` / `test result: FAILED. 16 passed; 1 failed`. Line 148 is `.expect("daemon start")` inside the `start_with` helper (tests/m3_execution.rs:135-149). Two earlier probe runs (with unrelated mutations in `domain/workspace.rs` and `domain/workflow.rs`) also showed single spurious failures — one in `m2_daemon_api`, one in `m3_execution` — which re-running cleanly did not reproduce. This means a green `cargo test` is weaker evidence than the ledger treats it as, and a red one can be noise. Also noted: a stale worktree `/tmp/probe-lock` at 5a60f49 is still registered in `git worktree list`, left by an earlier round, not by me.
confirmed.confirmed_because: Reproduced and root-caused, so it survives refutation. Probes (disposable worktree `/tmp/probe-flake` at HEAD 5a60f49, removed afterward; main tree untouched, `git status` clean): 12 serial `cargo test --test m3_execution` runs and 8 serial full `cargo test` runs were all green — so the flake is NOT reliably visible at low load, which is why a casual re-run looks clean. But under contention (3 rounds x 4 concurrent `cargo test --test m3_execution` processes on a 4-core box, separate --target-dirs) every round produced a failure at exactly the cited site, tests/m3_execution.rs:148:6 `.expect("daemon start")` in `start_with`, with the message `daemon start: Journal(Locked)`. It hit `a_crash_inside_the_submit_window_fails_closed_with_the_git_evidence` in 2 of 3 rounds and also `t6_cancel_mid_stage_leaves_no_zombie_work_state` and `t8_restart_resumes_unambiguous_work_and_blocks_ambiguous_work`, so the flake is not specific to the named test — it is any m3 test whose daemon start races. Mechanism: `Journal::open_with` (src/runtime/journal.rs:150-159) takes an exclusive advisory flock on `<data_dir>/journal/<LOCK_FILE_NAME>` and maps WouldBlock to `JournalError::Locked`; the flock belongs to the open file description, so a concurrently fork/exec'd `git` child (init_repo and the engine spawn git throughout this suite, and tests in one binary run on parallel threads) transiently duplicates the descriptor and can hold the lock past the parent's drop, widening under CPU contention into a spurious `Locked`. That is a genuine test-harness defect, not a product bug and not reporter error, and it does make a single green `cargo test` weaker gate evidence than the ledger treats it as. Two caveats on the write-up, neither touching the core claim: (a) the failure is a startup-lock race shared by several tests, not a property of the crash-evidence test; (b) the incidental note that a stale `/tmp/probe-lock` worktree at 5a60f49 is 'still registered in git worktree list' is false — `git worktree list` shows only the main tree plus another round's live `/tmp/probe-ponytail`, and no `/tmp/probe-lock` directory exists.

confirmed.summary: `cargo test` is not deterministically green at HEAD: the M3 suite fails roughly 5% of parallel runs with `daemon start: Locked`, and the tests that flake are precisely the restart/reconcile ones this axis depends on.
confirmed.evidence: Main tree, `cargo test --test m3_execution` in a loop: 2 failures in 40 runs (t6_cancel_mid_stage and t8_restart_...), plus earlier hits on t6, t8 and a_crash_inside_the_submit_window_fails_closed — all panicking at tests/m3_execution.rs:148 `daemon start: Locked` (DaemonError::Locked, src/daemon.rs:177) on the *second* start_with over the same data dir after `handle.shutdown().await`. Probe in a disposable worktree (/tmp/probe-lock, removed) instrumented the WouldBlock arm: at failure the target lock file's inode (1965951) had *no* entry in /proc/locks while four other tests' daemon.lock inodes did — i.e. the conflicting holder is transient (the shut-down daemon's lock outliving shutdown()'s return, or a duplicate of that open file description in a concurrently forked `git` child, which M3 introduced and M2 had none of).
confirmed.confirmed_because: Reproduced directly on the main tree at HEAD: `cargo test --test m3_execution` failed 8 of 40 default-parallelism runs (20%, worse than the claimed ~5%), every failure panicking at tests/m3_execution.rs:148 with `daemon start: Locked` (DaemonError::Locked from the TryLockError::WouldBlock arm at src/daemon.rs:177), and the flaking tests are exactly t6_cancel_mid_stage_leaves_no_zombie_work_state, t8_restart_resumes_unambiguous_work_and_blocks_ambiguous_work, and a_crash_inside_the_submit_window_fails_closed_with_the_git_evidence -- the restart/reconcile evidence this axis rests on; `cargo test --test m2_daemon_api` was 0/20 failures, confirming an M3-layer regression, and M3 does introduce forked git children (src/runtime/git.rs:75, src/runtime/surface.rs:473) that can duplicate the flock'd open file description in the fork->exec window, which defeats the otherwise-correct-looking scoping of `_lock` into the serve task (src/daemon.rs:252) awaited by DaemonHandle::shutdown (src/daemon.rs:124-129). GAUNTLET.md names plain `cargo test` as a gate for every prior milestone (lines 43, 53, 119, 177), so a suite failing one run in five is not deterministically green.
